Hello there! I wanted to share some thoughts from a recent classroom observation. One of the major strengths was how you used concrete models and everyday examples, like cake and shapes, to explain fractions. This really helped students understand the concept of parts-of-a-whole, and they were actively using the vocabulary and giving explanations in their responses.

Now, for a growth opportunity, I noticed that while you gave a lot of prompts to the students, there was room for more specific feedback. Next time, after a student identifies something like the numerator, you could add a step by saying, "Great, now tell me why that's the numerator." This approach will guide them to think deeper and connect their answers to the concept.

Keep up the great work, and remember, every step towards improvement makes a big difference. You're doing a fantastic job leading your class!
